headline: Mideast Headlines and Apple's Report Frame a Cautious Tuesday Open
body_html:
Investors face Tuesday's open with Middle East news pulling in two directions. Oil edged higher after reports of a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, which officials described as defensive. Yet Iran said contacts on ending the war continue despite talks that produced no breakthrough, and President Trump voiced doubts about fresh attacks. The dollar drifted as traders weighed that backdrop and the approaching midterm elections.

Monday's session was constructive underneath. Of 529 stocks tracked, 304 rose and 221 fell. Homebuilders led sectors with a 5.24% gain, ahead of industrials at 2.21% and consumer shares at 1.87%. Energy fell 3.21% and semiconductors dropped 2.38%. IDEXX Labs jumped 21.85% and Nextracker added 14.87%, while Marvell slid 12.72% and Ciena lost 11.34%.

At the open, watch whether oil holds its overnight uptick and whether energy can steady after Monday's slide. Also watch whether chip and optical names keep sliding or find buyers. Apple reports after the bell, with options traders pricing a large move. Prediction markets put the chance of Democrats winning the Senate near 75%, keeping politics in view.

briefs.headline: Oil Twitches on Reports of Strike Near Iran
briefs.body: Crude edged up overnight after reports of a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, which officials called defensive. Mixed signals followed, as Iran said talks ended without a breakthrough but contacts continue. Energy shares fell 3.21% on Monday, so the open will test whether crude's bounce holds.

briefs.headline: Chip and Optical Names Look for a Floor
briefs.body: Semiconductors lost 2.38% on Monday, led by sharp drops in Marvell, down 12.72%, and Ciena, down 11.34%. Okta and Everpure also fell more than 10%. Traders will watch whether the selling extends into Tuesday or dip buyers step in.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Lead a Cyclical Rally
briefs.body: Homebuilders surged 5.24% on Monday, the best showing among tracked sectors. Industrials rose 2.21% and consumer shares gained 1.87%. Thor Industries added 7.56%. The question now is whether the move carries on or pauses ahead of this week's events.

briefs.headline: Solar and Diagnostics Names Spark Big Gains
briefs.body: Nextracker climbed 14.87% and Enphase Energy rose 8.89%, putting solar-related shares among Monday's strongest performers. IDEXX Labs led all movers with a 21.85% jump. Insperity and Exponent also gained more than 7%, showing strength beyond the cyclicals.

briefs.headline: Apple Reports After the Bell
briefs.body: Apple is due to report after the close, and options traders expect a sizable move in the shares. That keeps the megacap in focus through the day. Positioning in technology could stay measured until the numbers arrive.

briefs.headline: Midterm Vote Looms Over Markets
briefs.body: The dollar drifted overnight as midterm risks joined Mideast concerns. Prediction markets see roughly a 75% chance that Democrats win the Senate. The Texas governor's race has tightened, though Governor Abbott is still favored.
